title: Affine completed-Hom evaluation before tensor comparison
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme, I a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, and F,G coherent modules [pqf-def-coherent]. Write H for the internal Hom from G to F [def-pur-sheaf-hom], and use the quotient systems and projections of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Suppose for every n there is a map e_n from H/I^(n+1)H to internal Hom(G/I^(n+1)G,F/I^(n+1)F), whose precomposition by the G quotient and by the H quotient equals postcomposition by the F quotient. For an affine open U [def-weil-affine-spectrum], put A = O_X(U), J = I(U), N = G(U), M = F(U), and B = the J-adic completion of A. Let epsilon be any B-linear map from the J-adic completion of Hom_A(N,M) to Hom_B(N-completion,M-completion) sending of(h) to the completed map h for every A-linear h. Then there is an equivalence rho from compatible families s of sections of H/I^(n+1)H over U to the J-adic completion of Hom_A(N,M). For every compatible family t_n of sheaf morphisms G/I^(n+1)G to F/I^(n+1)F there is a B-linear map v from N-completion to M-completion such that, for every s, all equations e_n(U)(s_n) = t_n restricted to U hold if and only if epsilon(rho(s)) = v. This assertion contains no tensor product or tensor/base-change comparison.

proof.text: Use the existing coherence criterion to install quasi-coherence and finite type for G and F. Apply the existing Scheme.Modules.finite_sections_of_finiteType theorem directly to make N and M finite; no coherent finite-section helper is restated. The linear-map module H is finite over the Noetherian affine section ring. The surjective tensor/completion map shows that completed H is generated over the completed ring by of(H). Tensor induction proves that completed-ring-linear maps agreeing on of(H) agree everywhere.

Obtain canonical quotient coordinates pN,pM from the affine section-coordinate theorem, and rho,E and the pointwise evaluation formula from the componentwise internal-Hom theorem. The previous generator-extensionality argument identifies the supplied epsilon with E.

For a compatible family t, apply t_n to pN_n(x). Compatibility of t and pN gives a compatible family of F quotient sections. The universal property of pM gives w(x), uniquely determined by joint injectivity. Joint injectivity also proves additivity. At each level choose an ordinary representative of a completed scalar; both projection scalar laws and linearity of t_n prove B-linearity. This constructs v with pM_n(v(x))=t_n(U)(pN_n(x)).

If the local e_n(s_n) equations hold, the pointwise formula and the projections of v agree for every completed input, so joint injectivity of pM gives epsilon(rho(s))=v. Conversely, this map equality implies equality of pointwise evaluations after pM. Surjectivity of pN tests all quotient inputs, and injectivity of local Hom-section evaluation gives e_n(s_n)=the section of t_n. Both directions are real Lean proofs.

theorem completion_internal_hom_affine_completion_evaluation {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F G : CoherentModules X)
    (e : ∀ n : ℕᵒᵖ,
      formalModuleQuotient I (n.unop + 1) (SheafOfModules.homObj
        (R := X.toRingedSpace.sheaf) G.obj F.obj) ⟶
        SheafOfModules.homObj
          (R := X.toRingedSpace.sheaf) (formalModuleQuotient I (n.unop + 1) G.obj)
          (formalModuleQuotient I (n.unop + 1) F.obj))
    (he : ∀ n : ℕᵒᵖ,
        formalModuleQuotientπ I (n.unop + 1) (SheafOfModules.homObj
          (R := X.toRingedSpace.sheaf) G.obj F.obj) ≫
          e n ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap
            (R := X.toRingedSpace.sheaf) (formalModuleQuotientπ I (n.unop + 1) G.obj)
            (𝟙 (formalModuleQuotient I (n.unop + 1) F.obj)) =
        SheafOfModules.homObjMap
          (R := X.toRingedSpace.sheaf) (𝟙 G.obj) (formalModuleQuotientπ I (n.unop + 1) F.obj))
    (U : X.affineOpens) :
    let A := Γ(X, U.val)
    let B := AdicCompletion (I.ideal U) A
    let N := Γ(G.obj, U.val)
    let M := Γ(F.obj, U.val)
    ∀ ε : AdicCompletion (I.ideal U) (N →ₗ[A] M) →ₗ[B]
      (AdicCompletion (I.ideal U) N →ₗ[B] AdicCompletion (I.ideal U) M),
      (∀ h : N →ₗ[A] M, ε (AdicCompletion.of (I.ideal U) _ h) =
        AdicCompletion.map (I.ideal U) h) →
    ∃ ρ : {s : ∀ n : ℕᵒᵖ,
          (formalModuleQuotient I (n.unop + 1) (SheafOfModules.homObj
            (R := X.toRingedSpace.sheaf) G.obj F.obj)).val.obj (op U.val) //
          ∀ (a b : ℕᵒᵖ) (f : a ⟶ b),
            ((formalCompletionSystem I (SheafOfModules.homObj
              (R := X.toRingedSpace.sheaf) G.obj F.obj)).map f).val.app (op U.val)
              (s a) = s b} ≃ AdicCompletion (I.ideal U) (N →ₗ[A] M),
      ∀ (t : ∀ n : ℕᵒᵖ, formalModuleQuotient I (n.unop + 1) G.obj ⟶
        formalModuleQuotient I (n.unop + 1) F.obj),
        (∀ (a b : ℕᵒᵖ) (f : a ⟶ b),
          t a ≫ (formalCompletionSystem I F.obj).map f =
            (formalCompletionSystem I G.obj).map f ≫ t b) →
        ∃ v : AdicCompletion (I.ideal U) N →ₗ[B] AdicCompletion (I.ideal U) M, ∀ s,
          (∀ n : ℕᵒᵖ, (e n).val.app (op U.val) (s.val n) =
            ((SheafOfModules.homObjSectionsEquiv (R := X.toRingedSpace.sheaf)
              (formalModuleQuotient I (n.unop + 1) G.obj)
              (formalModuleQuotient I (n.unop + 1) F.obj)).symm (t n)).val (op U.val)) ↔
            ε (ρ s) = v
